narrative.overview:
A dark instrument for a bounded decision. Void grounds the interface, Graphite gives controls a quiet working surface, and bright Geist text keeps permissions and evidence readable. Electric Mint identifies the next action and the active signal; Signal Lime makes exceptions visible. The authored circuit mark, orthogonal wires, and actual eleven-NAND graph connect the identity to the mechanism the product exposes.

The landing brief gives the policy a broad stage and a large, tightly tracked headline. The workspace brief gives tasks more room than decoration: credit totals, bounded sessions, editors, and evidence form a measured reading order. These are two expressions of the same world; their compositions remain in the surface briefs. Motion is brief and driven by state, while phones, reduced-motion preferences, and graphics failures retain the authored SVG circuit.

This system records the current frontend source and sampled desktop/phone captures. Electric precision is the accepted visual-world pin; both layouts are builder-authored within the accepted frontend scope. The launch finish review records the validation state for the horizontal-header refresh and uses a fresh generic agent with the packaged review contract. No approved comp, QUALITY BAR card, catalog seed, or successful detector/context/seed launcher is claimed. The shipped mark and circuit use SVG and geometry; there are no browser-shipping raster plates. Implementation values below come from `apps/web/app/globals.css`, `apps/web/app/styles/landing.css`, `apps/web/app/layout.tsx`, and the shared components.
keyCharacteristics: Dark neutral layers with readable, slightly cool text.
Mint actions and active signals; Lime exceptions; Red denials and destructive intent.
Self-hosted Geist Sans for instructions and Geist Mono for measurable evidence.
Compact controls, fine borders, and shallow corners.
An actual circuit graph with explicit source, mask, and payment output.
Responsive task layouts and a usable SVG fallback.

rules.name: The Decision Color Rule
rules.body: Use the signal color with its text label. Mint can mean an active signal or a checked result; the label must say which. Lime marks an exception or special context, and Red states a denial, error, or destructive action.

rules.name: The Readable Neutral Rule
rules.body: Keep task titles and values in Ink, explanations in Muted, and auxiliary labels in Dim. The reviewed secondary-text samples reached at least (7.31:1); this is sampled evidence, not a claim about every possible color pairing.

rules.name: The Measured Data Rule
rules.body: Use Geist Mono with tabular numerals for code, masks, identifiers, and token amounts. Keep prose and control labels in Geist Sans. Preserve exact displayed amounts rather than converting them to approximate floating-point summaries.

rules.name: The Task Adjacency Rule
rules.body: Keep actions next to the record or limit they change: session controls beside session balances, run controls after budget context, and receipt links beside the request. Reflow that relationship when columns stack.

rules.name: The Tonal Surface Rule
rules.body: Use a tonal layer and a fine boundary for resting content. Reserve the observed soft shadows for temporary overlays.

rules.name: The Diagram Form Rule
rules.body: Gate shapes and wires must come from the actual netlist. They explain a decision; their geometry is not a generic card decoration.

rules.name: The Evidence Label Rule
rules.body: A ready result, a checked provider signature, and a canonical payment remain separate visible statements. Gateway-recorded circuit inputs stay labeled unconfirmed until their settlement is independently verified. Local-fork transactions and controlled offline AI output keep their explicit context labels.

rules.name: The State Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion follows the policy state. Keep the diagram, captions, condition labels, and explicit output usable when the graphics layer is absent.

dos: Do preserve the shared palette, font roles, shallow corners, and exact control states when extending a surface.
Do keep amounts and identifiers measurable with Mono, tabular numerals, full-value access, and explicit units.
Do pair semantic colors with readable state labels and keep result, signature, and payment evidence separate.
Do preserve the actual circuit topology, source caption, input mask, explicit decision text, and SVG fallback.
Do follow the existing responsive reflow, keep the active workspace link visible within its horizontal band, and let activity tables scroll within their own focusable region.
Do preserve labels, visible Mint focus, associated hints, native dialog behavior, and recoverable empty or offline states.
donts: Don't reuse a confirmed-payment label for a result, a provider claim, a pending transaction, or preview inputs.
Don't turn the landing composition into a required workspace layout.
Don't replace the authored circuit with an unrelated decorative graph or apply internal gate-label dimensions to general UI text.
Don't make an unlabeled color or a WebGL layer the only way to understand the payment decision.
Don't add resting card shadows to the recorded tonal surface system.
